top_problem: The body is not on the 12 pt baseline it claims to use. The 6 pt item gap is half a baseline, so item rows alternate between 5.25 and 11.25 pt off the grid measured from the deck top (118 pt). In row 1 the two columns drift apart: Brown Butter Old Fashioned sits at y 315.25 and Cognac VSOP at 321.25, and the House Originals subhead (306.25) is 6 pt off the Brandy subhead (312.25). La Botella also leaves a 102 pt dead hole, which the render's own check flags (no_card_more_than_12pt_empty = false). The boldest missing idea: the cards do not read as lotería cards. A real lotería card is a portrait card led by a big figure with the name under it, but here the figure is a 48 pt icon above a coloured bar and a list.

measurements.subhead_repeated_in_one_card: CLASSICS appears twice in El Cantarito (252.25 and 402.25)

fixes: Make the item gap 12 pt, or 0 with 12 pt leading throughout, and snap every subhead and card title to multiples of 12 pt from the deck top so that name and price baselines match across all four cards to within 0.3 pt.

Remove the 102 pt hole in La Botella: size row 1 to its content, swap the card widths so Botella takes the narrow column over a shorter row, or give the space to a larger figure; do not leave it as cream.
Merge the two CLASSICS groups in El Cantarito into one subhead (Margarita and Manhattan together, House Originals after them), because one subhead used twice in one card is a hierarchy error.

Commit to real lotería card anatomy: a large figure filling a portrait panel with the name bar under it, and an equal frame treatment on every card. Card 1 currently has a terracotta double frame with no ink rules on its name bar, while the other three have black rules.
Snap the four name bars' cap baselines (card titles at 4.24 and 10.24 pt off the grid) and the masthead title (0.5 pt off) to the same 12 pt grid so that the whole page shares one vertical rhythm.

top_problem: The header system breaks its own rules. In EL CANTARITO the subheader 'CLASSICS / Clásicos' appears twice, split by House Originals. The title bars are drawn two ways: El Cantarito's is a flat terracotta slab, while the other three have black top and bottom rules, and El Barril uses ink text where the others use cream. Subheaders get no more space above them than an ordinary item does: in the preview, the gap from the Margarita description to 'HOUSE ORIGINALS' is about 42 px, the same as the gap from the Brown Butter description to House Daiquiri. So the middle level of the hierarchy doesn't register. The boldest idea the design is missing: the lotería card should be the whole system, not a framed box on top of a list. Each card needs a proper numbered, full-bleed lotería face where figure, name and verse are one unit, and the list sits beneath it like the back of the card.

lens: palette, contrast, price and number styling
top_problem: The lotería idea is ownable, but it is executed as a tidy boxed list. The cards do not read as lotería cards: each figure is a 48 pt icon (14-17% of the card), the name sits above the list instead of in a band at the foot, and the numbers are small pink ordinals. The boldest missing idea is making each section a real portrait lotería card, with the cut-paper figure as the hero, the number big in the top corner, and the name band at the base. The prices are plain terracotta figures with nothing that ties them to the lotería concept. Measured: price right edges are exact (334.5 and 562.5 pt, ±0.0) and the format is consistently whole numbers with no $. Contrast passes WCAG 4.5:1 everywhere: terracotta prices 5.89 on card and 5.08 on featured, agave subheads 6.91 and 5.95, muted descriptions 7.78 and 6.70, ink on marigold bar 7.51. Loteria rosa on the featured card is only 4.66, which barely passes. Measured failure: no_card_more_than_12pt_empty = false, with 102 pt of dead space in La Botella, so criterion 5 is capped at 40. The bottom ink margin is 38.16 pt against 36 on the other sides (0.76 mm, within tolerance).
fixes: Rebuild each card as a true lotería card: a large cut-paper figure (at least 35% of the card), the number big in the top-left corner and the Spanish name in a band at the foot, then fill La Botella's 102 pt hole with this figure or by resizing the row instead of leaving it empty.

Give the numbers a system: set prices in Fraunces with a small rosa or terracotta ornament, or put the price in a tabla-style box so the prices tie into the lotería palette, and replace the rosa ordinals (4.66:1 on the featured card) with a darker shade or bigger lotería-style numerals.

Replace the harsh #231B16 black double frames on cards 2-4 with palette colours (agave, marigold and rosa frames to match each name bar) so the palette reads warm and deliberate rather than muddied by near-black boxes.
Make the featured card tint (#F3E3CB) clearly different from the cream page, or drop it, because right now it reads as a slightly dirty card rather than a spotlight.
Merge the two 'Classics / Clásicos' subheaders in El Cantarito into one group (Classics, then De la casa) so one subheader level does not repeat inside one card.

lens: design concept and elevating elements vs the best bar menus in the country
top_problem: The lotería idea is only a label here. Real lotería cards are about the image: a large central figure, a framed name cartouche at the foot and a number in the corner. These cards are ordinary bordered menu panels with a 48 pt clip-art icon (14-17% of the card height) and a coloured bar, and La Botella is 102 pt empty, which is a measured failure. The idea the design is missing is to make each card look like a real lotería card: a large, strong cut-paper figure, the name cartouche at the foot, the verse as the caller's line, and the drinks list set as the card's back or a side panel. That would make the tabla unforgettable instead of papel picado placed over four boxes.
fixes: Criterion 5, measured failure: rebalance the tabla so no card is more than 12 pt empty (no_card_more_than_12pt_empty = False; La Botella has 102 pt empty and La Rosa 30 pt). For example, give the spirits and wine cards a larger figure, or move Botella and Rosa into one right-hand column so the column heights match.

Scale the lotería figures up to at least 35-40% of each card and draw them as real two-colour lotería illustrations with a thin inner frame and the name cartouche at the foot. The current 48 pt icons read as generic clip art, not a lotería deck.

Merge the two 'CLASSICS / Clásicos' subheaders in El Cantarito into one (Margarita, then Manhattan), followed by 'House Originals'. Repeating the same subheader inside one card breaks the hierarchy and the reading order.

Cut the header stack on each card from five levels (ordinal, verse, figure, name bar, gloss) plus a rule down to three. Put the ordinal and verse inside the figure frame the way a real card does. Raise the 7.5 pt muted italic verse to at least 8.5 pt so it reads in bar light.

Give the masthead an ownable venue mark instead of the generic 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar' title. Space the papel picado string away from the title (the flags currently crowd the cap height) and let one lotería-card motif, rather than the stock papel picado, carry the brand.

top_problem: The lotería idea is only a label, not a card. Real lotería cards are mostly figure: a big central illustration inside a heavy frame, the number in a corner and the name set below the picture. Here the figure is a small 48 pt glyph (14-17% of the card height) sitting on top of an ordinary price list. On the phone this is plainer still: four framed boxes stacked one after another with a tab bar, and they read as a generic sectioned list, not a hand of cards dealt from a tabla. Measurements: the section 4 checks all pass. Printed margins are L36/T36/R36/B38.16 pt, and the 2.16 pt bottom overage is 0.76 mm, inside the 1 mm tolerance. Item-name left edges are 49.5/373.5 pt with zero variance. Price right edges are 334.5/562.5 pt with zero variance. Item gaps are 6.0 pt everywhere. Header rows line up across cards at 154/202/244/262 and 508/556/598/616 pt. Lotería rosa is 5.41:1 on the card and 4.66:1 on the featured card. The designer's own check no_card_more_than_12pt_empty is FALSE: La Botella has 102 pt empty at the foot and La Rosa has 30 pt. Phone: 390 px width, no horizontal scroll, sticky 2x2 tab bar, cards stacked in one column. However, dealt_rotation reports 'none' on all four cards, which contradicts the proposal's claim of tilted frames, so the 'dealt' phone gesture is not there.
fixes: Redraw each card as a real lotería card on both print and phone: make the figure 40-50% of the card, put the number in the top-left corner of a heavy frame, and set the name bar under the figure, with the list below as the card's 'reverse'. Keep the same proportions on the phone so the phone reads as the cards being dealt.

Fill or rebalance the 102 pt void in La Botella: give Añejo and the spirits more breathing room, move the 12 pt gutter or column split (for example 300/228), or let Botella and Rosa share a row height fitted to their content. Right now the print tabla is visibly lopsided, and the phone hides a problem the print shows.

Merge the Manhattan into the first Classics group (Margarita, Manhattan), then House Originals. At the moment 'CLASSICS Clásicos' appears twice in one card on both print and phone, which reads as an error.

Make the phone rotation real and visible (±1-1.5° on each card frame, alternating), or drop the claim. Also give the sticky 2x2 tab bar a clear active state (for example an inverted fill or a rosa underline), because at 390 px the four coloured chips all read as equally selected.

Raise the cantor verse from 7.5 pt italic muted to at least 9 pt, or set it as a curved or banner line on the card face. On the phone it is the one piece of cultural voice, and it currently looks like fine print.

lens: flow and section order for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: The flow breaks inside the lead card and across the grid. EL CANTARITO prints the 'CLASSICS / Clásicos' subheader twice (Margarita, then House Originals, then Clásicos again for the Manhattan). LA BOTELLA holds 3 thin items in the prime top-right slot and leaves 102 pt of empty space. And every non-cocktail description is a taxonomy stub ('Dry red wine.', 'A grape brandy.', 'The plata style of tequila.') with no ABV, region or age. The menu reads as one crafted cocktail card beside three placeholder cards.
problems: All 14 items and prices match build/draft_doc.json exactly (15/15/16/14, 12/16/18, 7/8/7/8, 12/11/13). Nothing is invented, changed or dropped, so criterion 9 is clean.

Section order moved from the draft's Cocktails > Beer > Wine > Spirits > Cider to Cocktails > Spirits > Beer & Cider > Wine. Putting agave second is defensible for a cantina, but proposal.md gives no note or rationale for the change.

In EL CANTARITO the Clásicos subheader appears twice and splits the classics around House Originals. The Manhattan (the least on-concept drink for a cantina) sits alone under a repeated header, and House Originals are sandwiched in the middle rather than featured.
LA BOTELLA (3 items) and LA ROSA leave large empty feet (max 102 pt), so the grid is unbalanced: the prime top-right slot is the weakest-content card.
Añejo Tequila prints with no description, and nothing on the menu or in doc.json shows a missing_ingredients flag. The proposal mentions a flag, but it is not visible on the item.

Beer descriptions have no ABV (the scorecard requires style + ABV). Wine descriptions have no region, and 'Dry red wine.' / 'Dry white wine.' only repeat the category. Cognac VSOP 'A grape brandy.' and Blanco 'The plata style of tequila.' are taxonomy wording, not guest language.
Tone is uneven: cocktail lines are rich single sentences, while beer, wine and spirits lines are 2-4 words, so the four cards do not read in one editorial voice.
Prices share one no-$, no-decimal format and a right edge per card. However, no glass/bottle labels exist for wine, and it is not stated whether the wine and spirit prices are glass or pour prices.
fixes: Merge the two Clásicos blocks into one (Margarita, Manhattan) and put House Originals first or last as the featured block, so each subheader appears once in EL CANTARITO.

Put a visible missing_ingredients flag on Añejo Tequila, and on every beer (ABV), every wine (region) and Cognac VSOP (age/house), in doc.json and in proposal.md's questions, rather than printing stubs or blanks.

Rewrite the non-cocktail lines from known facts only, in the cocktail voice (for example Pilsner: 'Czech-style pilsner, crisp and pale' plus ABV once supplied), and replace the taxonomy phrases 'A grape brandy.' and 'The plata style of tequila.'.

Rebalance the tabla so the thinnest card does not hold the prime top-right slot, or fill LA BOTELLA's 102 pt void with a serve note (for example neat or with sangrita, only if the venue confirms it), and add a one-line note in proposal.md justifying the Spirits-before-Beer order change from the draft.
Label the wine and spirit prices with their pour (glass / 2 oz) once confirmed, so every price column has a stated unit.

top_problem: The menu reads in two voices. Rewrite the spirits and wine lines as one-sentence guest copy built from the same verified facts (for example 'Tequila in its plata style: bright, clean agave.' only if every word is sourced; otherwise keep the fact but drop the category phrasing) and print a small 'details coming' mark on Añejo instead of a blank.

lens: how missing data is handled and flagged

All 14 items and prices match build/draft_doc.json, nothing is invented or dropped, and every gap has a missing_ingredients flag. But Añejo Tequila prints with no description at all: the draft line 'Añejo tequila pour.' was removed and nothing replaced it. Blanco ('The plata style of tequila.') and Cognac VSOP ('A grape brandy.') print database category wording rather than guest copy. Beer has no ABV and wine has no region, with no visible sign on the menu that these are still to come. Brut Rosé's $13 still has no glass or bottle label, so a guest cannot tell what the price buys. The result is rich cocktail copy next to thin or empty lines in the other three cards.
fixes: Give Añejo Tequila a printed line again: keep the draft wording or hold the card until the venue supplies brand and age; do not leave a name-only item on a publishable menu.

Resolve the Brut Rosé glass-or-bottle question with the venue before sign-off and print a pour label (for example 'glass' or 'bottle') next to the 13, because an unlabelled price under Espumoso is ambiguous.
Put the cocktail card in one clean order: Margarita and Manhattan together under a single Classics header, then House Originals. Right now the Classics subheader appears twice in El Cantarito.

Replace the category-wording spirit lines with draft-sourced guest phrasing, or add the category note only after the brand and age come back from the venue, so La Botella stops reading like a database and its 102 pt of empty space at the foot is filled with real facts.

Chase the venue for beer ABV and brewery, wine region and producer, and pour sizes in one consolidated needs_input request, and hold approval until they arrive, because criterion 8 cannot rise above about 60 while every beer and wine line is the three-word draft placeholder.

lens: trace printed ingredients, garnishes, glass, serve and spirit lines to sources
top_problem: The facts are clean, but the descriptions are not. Everything printed traces to a source: the gateway returned rows for recipe_versions (log 134) and beverage_categories (log 136). (c1ad100b / a88f6e79), 'Dry red wine.' and 'Dry white wine.' Añejo has no line at all. So the menu has two voices: full guest sentences for the cocktails and database classes for everything else. Nothing printed is invented. Points still lost: no pour size, ABV, producer, region or age statement anywhere; 'on the rocks' is inferred from glassware + method rather than printed in any row; 'Del agave' is awkward Spanish for a category label.
fixes: Replace the taxonomy lines 'The plata style of tequila.' and 'A grape brandy.', and the blank Añejo line, with guest-language copy once the venue supplies brand, age and pour; until then, keep 'Blanco tequila pour.' / 'VSOP Cognac pour.' from menu_items, or print name only for every spirit, so the card reads in one voice.

The 'Classics / Clásicos' subheader appears twice in El Cantarito (Margarita, then House Originals, then Classics again for the Manhattan); this split breaks coherence. Ask the designer to group the Margarita and Manhattan under one Classics head (layout note: this is an order change, not an edit to the item list).

Brut Rosé at 13 still has no glass or bottle label, and no pour size is given for the Por copa wines or the draft beer; print the label as soon as the venue answers, because an unlabelled wine price fails criterion 14.

La Botella has 102 pt of empty space at the foot while the cocktail and beer cards are full; that balance problem goes to the designer. The printed ordinals 1-4 can be mistaken for official lotería deck numbers (El Cantarito is not card 1); add a small note or drop the numerals so the cultural reference stays accurate.

lens: description quality and one guest voice
top_problem: The menu has two voices. The four cocktails get full guest sentences (spirit, modifiers, method, glass, garnish), but the other ten items read as data labels. 'The plata style of tequila.' and 'A grape brandy.' are beverage_categories taxonomy (rows 04d72e1f and a88f6e79) printed word for word. 'Hop-forward draft IPA.', 'Dry sparkling cider.' and 'Dry sparkling rosé.' mostly repeat the item name. 'Dry red wine.' and 'Dry white wine.' could describe any bottle, and Añejo Tequila has no line at all. That meets the criterion-12 automatic-fail wording (taxonomy wording and name repeats) for about half the list.
verified_sources: Gateway log_id 133 (phg.menu_items joined to phg.recipe_versions on current_recipe_version_id). Margarita rv f06abb74: Rocks, Lime wheel, 'Shake with ice and strain over fresh ice'. Brown Butter Old Fashioned rv 7095fd3d: Rocks, Orange peel, 'Stir with ice and strain over a large cube'. House Daiquiri rv 14d45e57: Coupe, Lime coin, 'Shake with ice and fine strain'. Manhattan rv 9fb77eaa: Coupe, Cocktail cherry, 'Stir with ice and strain'. Every printed cocktail ingredient, glass, garnish and method matches these rows plus the build/draft_doc.json components (Fresh Lime Juice, Agave Syrup, Demerara Syrup 'House 1:1', Rye Whiskey, Cocktail Cherry). The score is held at 80 because 'on the rocks' is inferred from the Rocks glass plus the method, 'served up' is inferred from the coupe, and the Manhattan's aromatic bitters (in recipe_components and menu_description 'Rye, sweet vermouth, aromatic bitters.') are left out pending venue sign-off.
problems: Criterion 12: the spirits lines are category-tree wording, not guest language ('The plata style of tequila.', 'A grape brandy.').

Criterion 12: the beer, cider and rosé lines restate the name (Dry-Hopped IPA / 'Hop-forward draft IPA.'; Dry Cider / 'Dry sparkling cider.'; Brut Rosé / 'Dry sparkling rosé.'). Malbec and Pinot Grigio get interchangeable 'Dry red/white wine.'

Criterion 12/10: the lengths are very uneven. Cocktails run about 20 words over two lines, everything else runs 3 to 5 words, and Añejo has none. The cocktail sentences also share one rigid formula ('X, Y and Z, shaken/stirred and served ... with a ...') that reads like a spec sheet rather than a bartender talking.
